hypothesis: Giving Claude Code (hermes -z) the team's 15 decisions via Mole's hooks, WITH a check that forces a fix on a blocking violation (a resume that actually happens, unlike v1 where it fired 0/17 times), raises weighted decision-compliance points on dcbench versus the same decisions pasted into CLAUDE.md (R) and versus no context (A).

arms.description: dcbench Config A as shipped: no CLAUDE.md, no Mole. Baseline, rerun from a pinned copy (v1's deviation, see FROZEN.sha256, is not repeated).
CLAUDE.md = the 15 decision texts from benchmark/seed-data.ts, verbatim (same text as M, v1's fairness rule unchanged).

The same 15 as .mole/decisions records + Mole's hooks, PLUS the v2 fix: a model-judge (haiku router) after the edit forces one resume on any blocking violation, instead of v1's model-free Stop check that never fired (0/17). Code is run from a pinned copy per arm, never the live working tree (v1's deviation fix).

primary_metric: weighted decision-compliance percentage (dcbench scorer.ts, unchanged), intention-to-treat
analysis_plan: paired permutation test (scipy.stats.permutation_test, permutation_type=samples, exact 2^8 sign flips) on the 8 per-task mean percentages, for each of R-M, A-M, A-R; Holm correction across the 3 p-values (statsmodels multipletests); bootstrap 95% CI (scipy.stats.bootstrap, percentile) on each arm's mean task percentage; clustered SE by task (Anthropic arXiv 2411.00640 Eq. 4); Newcombe 95% CI on the merge-ready rate difference per pair; report R vs M first, losses first, as v1 did. Significance bar: p < 0.05 on the primary paired permutation test (v1 found R-M p=1.0, A-M p=0.375, A-R p=0.5 -- all not significant).
stop_rules: any edit to scorer.ts, tasks.ts, the R CLAUDE.md or the M records after run 1: a NEW spec version (v3), all arms rerun
quoting dcbench's own published Config B numbers beside this experiment's A/R/M as if they were one experiment (different harness: their runner spawns `claude`, this one spawns `hermes -z`)

a merge to plugins/claude-code/scripts/* or packages/daemon mid-run without re-pinning the per-arm code copy (v1's deviation, logged in FROZEN.sha256, must not recur: v2 runs arms from a pinned copy, never the live tree)
